app-for-meeting-minutes.0: An app for meeting minutes has one job. It should produce a record of who attended, what was decided and who owns what next. Most AI note takers produce summaries, but fewer produce something you could paste into a board pack or a project log without editing.
app-for-meeting-minutes.1: Below, we compare 8 apps US teams use for minutes, explain which ones fit Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, iPhone and Mac, and show what good AI-generated minutes should contain. Need the format itself? See our [meeting minutes sample](https://lynkk.ai/blog/meeting-minutes-sample).
app-for-meeting-minutes.2: A good app for meeting minutes captures 5 things automatically: attendees, agenda topics, decisions, action items with owners and dates, and the next meeting. A transcript alone falls short. You still have to write the minutes.
app-for-meeting-minutes.5: Lynkk records online meetings through a bot on Zoom, Google Meet and Teams, and in-person or bot-free meetings through its Mac app and Chrome extension. After each meeting you get structured notes, tasks with owners and dates, and a decision log. Together, that covers what formal minutes need.
app-for-meeting-minutes.6: Languages: 17, Hindi and Hinglish included. Free covers 5 notes a month at up to 2 hours each, and Pro costs $15 a month.
app-for-meeting-minutes.8: If your company pays for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams can generate AI recaps with notes and follow-up tasks from recorded or transcribed meetings. Teams meetings only, though. No Copilot license? See [Teams AI note takers](https://lynkk.ai/blog/ai-note-taker-microsoft-teams) for options.
app-for-meeting-minutes.9: Gemini in Google Meet writes notes into a Google Doc saved in the organizer's Drive, but it needs an eligible Workspace edition or Google AI plan. Languages? 8 are supported, one per meeting ([Google Meet help](https://support.google.com/meet/answer/14754931)).
app-for-meeting-minutes.10: Fathom records unlimited calls with transcripts and AI summaries for free on Zoom, Google Meet and Teams. Want better action items and CRM sync? Paid plans add both, from $16 a month billed yearly ([Fathom pricing](https://www.fathom.ai/pricing)).
app-for-meeting-minutes.11: Otter shows a live transcript and writes a summary after. The catch? Free caps each conversation at 30 minutes, which rules it out for most formal meetings. Pro allows 90 minutes for $8.33 billed yearly.
app-for-meeting-minutes.12: Fireflies writes summaries and pushes them into CRMs and other tools, with Pro at $10 per seat billed yearly. Compare it in [Otter vs Fireflies vs Fathom](https://lynkk.ai/blog/otter-ai-vs-fireflies-ai).
app-for-meeting-minutes.13: No bot here. Notion's note taker writes meeting notes into a Notion page from the desktop app, and it comes included on the Business plan at $20 per member. See our [Notion note taker review](https://lynkk.ai/blog/notion-note-taker).
app-for-meeting-minutes.14: Read AI adds engagement and talk-time metrics to summaries. Free covers 5 meetings a month. Pro? $15 billed yearly.
app-for-meeting-minutes.15: Bot-based apps join the meeting as a participant and record from inside the call, while bot-free apps capture audio on your own device. Both work. They just suit different meetings.
app-for-meeting-minutes.16: Lynkk (our product) offers both: a bot for Zoom, Google Meet and Teams, and bot-free recording through its Mac app and Chrome extension. In formal meetings such as boards and HOAs, a visible recorder often helps. Everyone knows the meeting is on the record.
app-for-meeting-minutes.18: Built-in recording gives you a video and sometimes a transcript, not minutes, so someone still has to turn it into decisions and actions. An app for meeting minutes saves that step. Step-by-step help: [how to record a Google Meet call](https://lynkk.ai/blog/record-google-meet-call).
app-for-meeting-minutes.20: Then test 2 apps on the same 3 meetings and compare the minutes side by side. Pick the one you edit least. Usually, that is the right choice.
app-for-meeting-minutes.24: Recording in person? Put the phone or laptop in the middle of the table, close to the people speaking, because room audio is the biggest factor in transcript accuracy, more than the app itself.
app-for-meeting-minutes.27: An AI app can replace the typing, not the judgment. Who said what, the draft decisions, the actions: AI captures all of it in minutes, but a person should still check names, motions, vote counts and anything legally sensitive before minutes are approved.
app-for-meeting-minutes.28: Board, HOA or LLC meeting? Treat AI output as a draft. Our guides to [board minutes](https://lynkk.ai/blog/board-minutes-of-meeting) and [LLC meeting minutes](https://lynkk.ai/blog/llc-meeting-minutes-template) cover what must be in the final record.

app-for-meeting-minutes.32: Yes. Fathom offers unlimited free recordings and AI summaries, with no monthly cap. Otter, Read AI and Lynkk also have free plans, but with monthly limits: Otter allows 300 minutes, Read AI 5 meetings and Lynkk 5 notes of up to 2 hours each. That is enough for a weekly board or team meeting.
app-for-meeting-minutes.34: Yes. Otter, Granola and Jamie have iPhone apps that record in-person meetings and write notes. Lynkk works on Mac and in the browser. In person, place the phone in the middle of the table, since room audio affects accuracy more than which app you choose.
app-for-meeting-minutes.36: Meeting minutes should include the date, attendees, agenda items, decisions, action items with owners and due dates, and the next meeting date. Formal minutes also record motions and votes. Keep each agenda item to 2 to 4 lines; anything longer usually belongs in the meeting notes, not the official minutes.
